newsitem.title: USA: Boulder officials seek cooperation with Ramseys.
newsitem.headline: Boulder officials seek cooperation with Ramseys.

text.p: Officials investigating the murder of slain beauty pageant winner JonBenet Ramsey took a conciliatory step toward the child's parents Thursday, saying they want to cooperate with them.

In a letter to the parents' attorneys, which was released to the media, Boulder police and District Attorney Alex Hunter said they can "understand the feelings of frustration experienced by your clients."

On Wednesday, attorneys for the parents, John and Patricia Ramsey, said police cancelled interviews that had been scheduled with their clients and accused officials of waging a "smear" campaign against them.
The police department letter said officials "acknowledge the unfortunate miscommunication" that has developed.

No arrests have been made and no suspects named in the murder. The 6-year-old child's body was found Dec. 26 by her father in the basement of the family's home, about eight hours after her mother said she found a ransom note demanding $118,000.

But the police reiterated several conditions they deem necessary to conduct the interviews. For instance, they insist on interviewing the parents separately, and the mother first. Police refuse to put a time limit on the interviews, which will be tape recorded. Police have agreed to conduct the interivews at a "neutral location."

In a statement released later, the parents' attorneys said they are still concerned that the interviews were cancelled, but that they also believe most members of the Boulder Police Department and the District Attorney's office want to find the girl's killer.
